rubric.why: The carat value gives the number of parts of pure gold out of 24 parts.
rubric.description: States that 22 out of 24 parts are pure gold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct proportion.

rubric.why: The remaining parts are other metals, so 22-carat gold is an alloy.
rubric.description: Identifies the remaining 2 parts as other metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the remaining proportion or the presence of other metals.

modelAnswer: 22-carat gold contains 22 parts of pure gold out of 24 parts, so its purity is 22/24.
The remaining 2 parts (2/24) are other metals, such as copper or silver; therefore, 22-carat gold is an alloy.

items.followUp: Write any five properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: These properties identify the positive charge of canal rays and their deflection in an electric field.
rubric.description: States that canal rays are positively charged and are deflected towards the negative plate.

rubric.why: These properties describe the path of canal rays and their passage through the cathode.
rubric.description: States that canal rays travel in straight lines and pass through holes in a perforated cathode.

rubric.why: The gas in the discharge tube determines the positive ions and affects their charge-to-mass ratio.
rubric.description: States that the charge-to-mass ratio of canal rays depends on the gas present.

modelAnswer: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
In an electric field, they are deflected towards the negative plate.
They pass through the holes in a perforated cathode.
Their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the gas present in the discharge tube.

items.followUp: Write the steps for writing the formula of magnesium chloride.

rubric.why: The symbols identify the elements in the compound and their order in the formula.
rubric.description: Writes the symbols of the elements in the correct order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Mg followed by Cl.

rubric.why: The valencies are needed to determine the formula subscripts.
rubric.description: Writes the correct valencies of the elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Mg valency 2 and Cl valency 1.

rubric.why: Interchanging the valencies gives the initial subscripts in the formula.
rubric.description: Interchanges the valencies and writes them as subscripts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the criss-cross step.

rubric.why: The final formula uses the simplest whole-number ratio, with a subscript 1 omitted.
rubric.description: Writes the final formula with the subscript 1 omitted.

modelAnswer: Write the symbols of the elements in the compound in the correct order: Mg and Cl.
Write their valencies: Mg = 2 and Cl = 1.
Interchange the valencies and write them as subscripts: Mg₁Cl₂.
Remove the subscript 1 to obtain the formula MgCl₂.

items.followUp: Define molecular formula and give an example.

rubric.why: An empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.

rubric.why: Glucose has molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ and empirical formula CH₂O.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of an empirical formula.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
For example, glucose has molecular formula C6H12O6 and empirical formula CH2O.
